newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ's dollar's uptrend arrested this yr.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ's dollar's uptrend arrested this yr.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters, commenting on two surveys showing falling confidence in the New Zealand economy, said more attention should be paid to the recent stabilisation of the New Zealand dollar.
"They tell me they are concerned about the rise of the dollar, we'll let's have some credit being given where it is due," he told Radio New Zealand.
"The dollar has been arrested and since January has been stable. That's not been the pattern of the last three years."
"Various forecasts at the time (that) these surveys (were) being done had inflation at a much higher rate. Inflation is (now) dramatically down from those forecasts," Peters said.
Some of the confidence surveys seemed to have been done at the extreme end of calculations, he added.
Earlier, the National Bank in its monthly Business Outlook said that, excepting a period surrounding last year's general election, business confidence was at its lowest for six years.

The New Zealand Institute of Economic Research, in its quarterly business opinion survey, said the postponement of tax cuts planned for 1997 had quashed hopes of a consumption-led recovery and implied an upturn was not yet under way.
"Positive signs of economic activity in this survey are few and far between," the NZIER said.

In its April quarterly survey of business opinion, a net 9 percent of businesses surveyed expect the general business situation to deteriorate over the next six months, against a net 8 percent who expected an improvement in the previous survey.
